newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit up on technical rally.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit up on technical rally.

text.p: Early profit taking from an initial limit gain failed to attract outside selling interest and CME lumber futures ran up again late on technical demand to close up the limit of $10.00 per tbf in May, traders said.
May closed limit up at $373.70 per tbf while July finished up $7.30 at $368.20. Other months ended up $4.00 to $2.50.
There were some reports of a little better cash activity, but not enough to raise prices, they added.
"If retailers are truly in need of wood right now, we will find out in the next day or two," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Schmaedick considered the rally to be mostly technical in nature. The market will break after filling gaps in the chart around $380 if cash markets fail to firm up, he said.

May ran back up the limit within the last 10 minutes of trade as technicians continued to support the market. There were buy stops hit above Friday's high of $366 and again above $370, basis May, in early trade and futures drifted back up the limit on mixed demand late, they said.
